To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that the nested control problem can be reduced to an equivalent non-nested problem, that we have shown how to design controllers to stabilize a nested system in the presence of uncertainty and noise, and that we have developed a procedure that can be used to design controllers to ensure that the system is stable in spite of the uncertainty and noise.

(i) a nested control architecture is proposed that stabilizes a plant with uncertain communication channels, (ii) a controller architecture that stabilizes a nested control system with uncertain communication channels is proposed, (iii) a controller synthesis procedure for deterministic uncertainty is proposed, (iv) a controller synthesis for stochastic uncertainty is proposed, and (v) the controller synthesis procedures are illustrated with numerical simulations.

(i) a nested system can be stabilized with uncertain subsystem communication, provided that the uncertainty is not too great, and (ii) the uncertainty can be stochastic in nature, modeling packet-loss in the internet, and still be handled by our controller design procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the design of distributed controllers that stabilize nested systems in the presence of uncertainty.
a new approach to control of nested systems, where the control architecture is distributed and the communication channels are subject to noise and packet-loss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the presence of uncertainty in the communication channels, it is necessary to design a controller for each subcontroller, and not a single controller for all of them.
the design of a controller that can stabilize a nested system with uncertain communication channels is a challenging problem.
the design of a stabilizing controller for a nested control systems with uncertain channels is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the nested control system can be stabilized even when the nest-to-nested communication channel is subject to uncertainty.
we have shown that the controller architecture can tolerate the presence of uncertainty and noise in the plant, controller and communication channels.
we have developed a systematic approach to the design of controllers for nested systems, where the controllers are implemented in a distributed fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of stabilizers for nested systems is not necessarily complicated, and can be done in a modular fashion.

the presence of uncertainty and noise in the nest-to nest communication channel can be handled with the same controller architectures that have been used to handle controller-to-plant uncertainty and noise.
a nested system can be made robust against packet-loss in the communication channel by using a particular controller architecture.
